text: Ellie (design): quick sync on the 'Provision VM' form. two decisions: 1) error surfacing for dense/rowed inputs — do we show inline error text immediately, or do a collapsed error sweep at the top with anchors? 2) how explicit should the required indicator be? asterisk only feels terse. Rohan (pm): for power flows where users paste lots of rows, top sweep + anchors wins imo. inline noise makes the page feel broken. for single-item flows inline immediate feedback is nicer. Tess (frontend): technical note: rendering inline error s for every cell is expensive on mobile. we can render the summary first and mount inline nodes lazily when a row receives focus or when a user clicks the anchor. cheap compromise. Jun (a11y): asterisk alone is problematic. screen readers may skip it. recommend visible "Required" text or set aria-required=true and also expose a short legend for sighted users. if we keep the asterisk, include a visually-hidden clarifier: e.g., Required tied via aria-describedby. Ellie (design): microcopy ideas: current error: "Name missing". alternatives: "Please add a display name." or more contextual: "Please add a display name so your team can identify this VM." which is better? Rohan (pm): keep it short but helpful: "Please add a display name." Good balance. Tess (frontend): on destructive flows: typed-confirm modal (type resource name) vs lightweight undo toast. Suggest typed-confirm for irreversible deletion (customer data snapshots), undo toast for soft-delete workflows with retention. also consider rate limits for bulk undo operations. Jun (a11y): typed-confirm is okay if we provide clear SR instructions and focus management. announce the exact phrase required and focus the input. avoid modals that trap focus without announcing context (use role=dialog and aria-modal). Ellie (design): proposed pattern: summary-first after submit with a concise header like "We found 3 problems" + anchor links; inline detail appears on focus or after blur. Required marker: show a small asterisk visually + the word "Required" in helper text linked via aria-describedby, and a tooltip on hover for sighted users. Rohan (pm): sounds good. also define a threshold for bulk vs single destructive actions (e.g., >50 items -> bulk path with undo toast). Tess (frontend): implementation approach: add aria-live="polite" to the summary container, but don't auto-focus. anchors should move focus only when clicked. lazy-mount inline error nodes to keep initial render light. I'll prototype a component PR. Jun (a11y): add that the summary should contain a skip-link target so keyboard users can jump to the first error. when an anchor is used, move focus to the related input and ensure a short aria-live message announces the field name and error. Ellie (design): tone for the summary header: "We found X problems" vs "There are X errors" vs "Please fix these items". which is least harsh? Rohan (pm): "We found X problems" is neutral and user-friendly. Tess (frontend): +1. also recommend inline helper for critical fields: "Required used to route traffic" (we can fine-tune later). Ellie (design): quick poll: react :one: for inline-eager, :two: for summary-first (summary then inline-on-focus). DeployBot: New reactions: :eyes:. Jun (a11y): vote :two:. summary-first reduces cognitive load for assistive tech users when forms are long. Rohan (pm): :two:. Tess (frontend): :one: (but flexible). Ellie (design): looks like summary-first wins. i'll mock both variants (summary-first prototype + inline-eager) and run a 5-person usability quick test with one screen-reader user. will tag @Tess for the feasibility notes and @Jun for the a11y checklist before merge. Tess (frontend): i'll aim for a prototype branch tomorrow and stress test with a 300-row fixture. Jun (a11y): i'll prepare a small checklist: NVDA, VoiceOver, focus order, aria-live behaviour, skip-links. Ellie (design): thanks team — will post mocks by EOD. :sparkles:
